- Flag edited PR comment `/review` and `/fix-pr` commands during context extraction
- Post a clear portal response instead of silently skipping downstream PR actions
- Suppress eyes/status signals for these blocked edited-comment commands

Closes #437

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: ac9ab8bb19a9adaca19dac487a286f736bb4989c -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #438 addresses issue #437, where edited PR comments that add `@sepo-agent /review` or `/fix-pr` could look acknowledged but never dispatch because the downstream PR jobs skip `edited` events. The PR adds context outputs for this blocked case, posts a visible explanation, and suppresses misleading eyes/status signals. It also documents the behavior and adds focused extractor/workflow coverage. The implementation keeps the existing route authorization and edited-event job guards in place.

## Review
The core approach is correct and well scoped, and two review artifacts found no blocking issues. One current, actionable warning remains: the new explanation can be posted repeatedly or misleadingly because the implementation does not check whether the command was newly introduced by the edit.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Repeated edited-command explanations | WARNING | The new response step fires for every edited comment whose current body parses as `/review` or `/fix-pr`, so repeated edits can post duplicate explanations and edits to an already-actioned command comment can tell the user to repost unnecessarily. |
| Workflow job guards are not locked by tests | INFO | The feature relies on the `review` and `fix-pr` jobs continuing to skip `github.event.action == 'edited'`, but current workflow-shape coverage does not assert those two job guards directly. |

## Progress
- PR implements the conservative issue #437 path: keep edited-comment PR-modifying commands blocked, but explain the block visibly.
- Codex review reported `npm --prefix .agent run build` and focused node tests passing on PR head `ac9ab8bb19a9adaca19dac487a286f736bb4989c`.
- Rubrics review passed with no rubric-specific findings.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before mutation.
- Posted one inline warning on `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml:451`; no replies, minimizations, or thread resolutions were performed.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Repeated edited-command explanations</summary>

**Cause:** [`isEditedCommentPrCommandBlocked`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/ac9ab8bb19a9adaca19dac487a286f736bb4989c/.agent/src/cli/extract-context.ts#L63) checks `payload.action === "edited"`, target kind, event type, and route, but does not compare `changes.body.from`. The workflow step at [`.github/workflows/agent-router.yml:451`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/ac9ab8bb19a9adaca19dac487a286f736bb4989c/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L451) then posts a fresh response for each matching edit.

**Candidate solutions:** Gate the flag on the command being newly introduced by the edit, using `changes.body.from`, or dedupe/upsert a single explanation comment. Add regression coverage for repeated edits and edits where the command already existed before the edit.

**Comments:** This is not a blocker to the overall design, but it is a user-facing noise regression from idempotent reactions to potentially repeated top-level comments.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Workflow job guards are not locked by tests</summary>

**Cause:** The new behavior assumes the `review` and `fix-pr` jobs keep `github.event.action != 'edited'`; current tests assert the new explanation and signal-suppression wiring, but not those job-level guards.

**Candidate solutions:** Add workflow assertions for `jobs.review.if` and `jobs['fix-pr'].if` requiring `github.event.action != 'edited'`.

**Comments:** This is hardening coverage, not evidence of a current behavior failure.
</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The duplicate/misleading edited-comment response is a concrete branch change and is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Gate or dedupe the edited-comment explanation so repeated edits, or edits to command comments that already ran on creation, do not post duplicate or misleading responses.
